extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, photographers and other media professionals; newsrooms and media organizations interested in constructive/solutions journalism
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and guiding principles for producing and integrating constructive (solutions-focused) journalism across newsrooms, including aims, outcomes, and examples of implementation and training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace solutions, nuance and dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journalism embraces solutions, nuance and dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is framed as the core definition/mission: reporting should include solution-oriented coverage, pay attention to complexity rather than simplistic narratives, and foster dialogue (between journalists and audiences or among stakeholders). The site positions this as what constructive journalism 'is' and what should be brought into newsrooms worldwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide facts, uncover problems, and inspire potential solutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent journalism ... provides facts. Uncovers problems. And inspires potential solutions to the challenges facing all of us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should balance empirical factual reporting and problem-identification with journalism that points toward possible responses or solutions — not advocacy but inspiration for potential remedies. This three-part formulation is presented as the functional role of constructive journalism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize better news over more news
rubrics_metrics.description: Today, people do not need more news, they need better news. That's what we call constructive journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality (depth, usefulness, constructive orientation) is favored over volume/frequency. Implicit anti-pattern: producing high quantities of purely negative/attention-capturing stories without improving informational value or public utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain editorial independence
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent journalism is the core of society's conversation and progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive journalism must be carried out by independent outlets; independence is presented as foundational to credibility and to being part of democratic solutions rather than partisanship or sponsorship-driven messaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and demonstrate reader impact (wellbeing, credibility, empowerment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims and metrics: '73% of top news executives say constructive journalism is important to combat news avoidance and fatigue'; 'Readers feel 87% better after reading a constructive article...'; 'Constructive news leads to 8% higher credibility for media outlets...'; 'Readers feel 20% more empowered after reading a constructive article...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use audience outcome metrics (reduced avoidance/fatigue, improved emotional response, credibility lift, empowerment) to evaluate the effectiveness of constructive pieces and to justify newsroom adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate constructive practices into newsroom culture and formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples cited: 'Transforming newsroom culture', 'Rethinking journalism formats', 'Reviving local journalism'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructive journalism is not a one-off story type but should be embedded into daily workflow, editorial culture and formats. Implementation guidance includes fellowships, workshops, and training (the site lists workshops and a fellowship program) to change practices and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborate across disciplines and sectors
rubrics_metrics.description: We work with journalists, educators, researchers, tech innovators, philanthropists and others to create that solution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective constructive journalism involves cross-sector partnerships — leveraging research, education, technology and funding/philanthropy — to design, evaluate and scale constructive approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate global applicability through exemplar partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Born in Denmark, constructive journalism has proved to work across the globe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite and learn from international examples (the site highlights ZEIT ONLINE, The Guardian, Zetland, Public Interest Journalism Lab, etc.) to adapt constructive practices to different cultural and newsroom contexts rather than treating it as specific to one market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support implementation with programs, training and fellowships
rubrics_metrics.description: The Constructive Institute runs fellowships and heads workshops for journalists and editors (examples: fellowship cohorts, workshops in Croatia, Asia Pacific Hub fellowship program in Australia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational support (fellowships, workshops, hubs) is a recommended mechanism to build capacity for constructive journalism in newsrooms; adoption should include professional development and sustained support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use evidence-based storytelling and communication
rubrics_metrics.description: The site presents research-backed claims and outcomes for constructive journalism and features videos and interviews with practitioners and researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt an evidence-driven approach: document outcomes, use research to design constructive stories, and share examples and case studies (videos, published examples) as part of quality assurance and advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster audience engagement and dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructive journalism embraces ... dialogue (and the site encourages 'Get involved' and features audience-facing content and examples).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should open spaces for civic engagement and conversation, not just present solutions unidirectionally. This includes formats that invite audience participation, discussion, and local relevance (e.g., reviving local journalism).
